title: Divide Ladder
description: Climb a number one trial at a time, keep every rung that fails, and watch each exact division hand you two factors.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit.

bands.footer: 758 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it, the phase dots and the phase and question counts at the right.

writeup.why: Find every factor of a number by dividing by each whole number in turn, and find out why the run must not skip one.
writeup.look: A ladder of rungs up the middle with a tray of countable things above it, a shelf for whatever will not fit, and a fenced pen of factor cards beside it.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Divide Ladder' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name by measuring it, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and again, sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at 64,108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: the rungs tried against the rungs the ladder is built for, two numbers in ink, the first climbing by one as each trial settles and the second fixed at the height of the ladder, with the number of cards standing in the pen beside them. Nothing in it ever counts down and nothing in it ever reads as a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at 64,202. The ladder stands up the middle of the working area, 180 wide by 528 at 508,202, its rungs 56 tall and numbered from one at the foot upward, with the number tray above it at 508,202 holding the chosen number drawn as that many identical countable things, never more than twenty under one visible tie. Stepping on a rung opens the sharing board to the right of the ladder, 462 by 400 at 700,202: the tray empties onto it as that many rows, drawn genuinely equal and genuinely countable, each row shut off from the next by a drawn wall rather than by a change of colour. Where the sharing does not come out, whatever will not fit travels to the leftover shelf, 462 by 92 at 700,618, which sits OUTSIDE the rows on the same surface at full strength and fully countable, is never faded, never crossed out and never tucked under a row, and holds what it was given for the rest of the run. A rung tapped while a lower rung is still untried does not open: the untried rung lights, is named, and nothing else is given away, so the refusal teaches the order rather than the answer. Every rung that comes out sends two cards into the factor pen, 424 by 400 at 64,202, one carrying the number stepped on and one carrying the number in each row; the pen has a wall at its left end and a wall at its right and the cards lie in order between them, so the list is drawn closed while it is still being built. The repeat light sits above the pen at 64,142, dark until a card lands on one already inside, and the ladder stops climbing the instant it comes on. The tick and cross bay runs along the foot of the working area, 1086 by 76 at 64,654: a smaller number and a bigger one are dropped into it, one division runs on the board, and a tick or a cross is drawn with the remainder standing beside it. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at 1186,250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at 1170,368 (388 by 363). The pad is twelve number keys three across wherever a quotient, a remainder or a count of factors is asked for, and on the first phase a word pad of the ladder's own words, factor, divides, exactly, leftover, remainder and nothing over, so that a trial can be judged with one press. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own: a number that divides another exactly is deep blue, a number built by multiplying is green, anything standing in both lists at once is rose, whatever is left over and any trial that fails is vermilion, the number being broken up or the total in hand is amber, and a single digit being read or added is sky blue. Chrome never borrows one of those and none of them is ever used for chrome, and every reading survives with the colour taken away, because a trial that failed is told by the leftover standing outside its rows before it is told by a band, and a list that stops is told by the wall at each end of it before it is told by anything else. A rung that failed is never dimmed and never cleared as the ladder climbs past it. Its rows and its leftover stay drawn where they were, because a run with its failures rubbed out looks exactly like a run that never made them, and that likeness is the whole trouble with the page this tool is built from.
writeup.finish: The card shows the tallest ladder the child climbed, every failed rung with its leftover still showing, and the full pen beside it.

phases.win: one rung lights with level rows and the other leaves its remainder standing outside them
phases.does: steps on each rung in turn and looks at what is left on the shelf
phases.goal: a factor divides the number and leaves nothing over
phases.says: Share them out. Which try left nothing over? That one is a factor.
phases.check: Away from the screen: share 20 counters onto 4 plates, then onto 6. Which of those two numbers is a factor of 20, and how did the counters tell you?
phases.feels: a trial that leaves something over has answered, and the thing it left is the answer
phases.hands: Put twenty counters on the table and share them onto four plates, one at a time, going round. Then sweep them up and share the same twenty onto six plates the same way. Both times, before anybody says an answer, put whatever will not go round again in the middle of the table where everyone can see it and count it out loud. Ask which of the two numbers is a factor of twenty, and what the pile in the middle has to say about the other one.
phases.tries: A miss is answered three ways at once and none of them is the answer. First rung, from the item's own miss line: how many things are standing outside the rows? Second rung, the phase's: what does anything standing outside the rows say about this trial? Third rung: the tray is cut to twelve things and the child steps on three and then on five and looks at both shelves. The word pad stays open behind all three rungs.

wrong.why: two left out of twenty looks like a rounding off rather than a failure, and once they are out of sight the six rows sitting there look every bit as finished as the four rows did.
wrong.move: calls six a factor of twenty because it very nearly went in, and brushes the two that would not fit off the side of the tray.
wrong.screen: the sharing runs again at walking pace and the two are carried to the leftover shelf outside the rows, at full strength and countable, where they stay. The six rows are then counted out one at a time, three in each, and the board is read as eighteen; the tray it came from is read as twenty. The child's verdict stays in the answer slot the whole time and nothing is marked.

wrong.why: sharing has meant everybody getting some for as long as they have been sharing anything, and two things left over read as a problem to be tidied away rather than as the answer to the question.
wrong.move: shares the two left over out as well, splitting them between the rows so that every row comes out the same.
wrong.screen: the two are drawn whole and set on the shelf, and the rows are rebuilt from the tray with only whole things in them. The tool asks how many whole things went into each row and the board answers three, with the two still standing outside; the four plate sharing is then laid beside it with its shelf empty, and the two boards are left standing together.

phases.screen: a full tray with two rungs offered, one that comes out and one that does not
phases.soWhat: A factor divides the number and leaves nothing over, and anything standing outside the rows says it is not one.
phases.concept: What makes a number a factor

phases.win: every rung carries either level rows or a leftover, and no rung is blank
phases.does: climbs one rung at a time and tries to jump one, which is refused
phases.goal: the run is unbroken, and a trial that fails is still written down
phases.says: Start at the bottom and take every rung. Try to jump one and see what happens.
phases.check: The book's own run goes 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9. Which number never got a line, and what does 18 shared into that many rows leave?
phases.feels: a run with a hole in it looks exactly like a run without one
phases.hands: Write the factor pair run for eighteen out on squared paper exactly as the page prints it: one times eighteen, two times nine, three times six, then four fails, then six, seven, eight and nine. Read the run aloud and ask which whole number never got a line. Work that missing line together, eighteen shared into five rows, and write it in where it belongs. Then find the factors of forty the same way, with a line for every whole number from one to ten and not one of them left out.
phases.tries: First rung, from the item: which is the lowest rung with nothing written on it yet? Second rung, the phase's: can a number you never tried be ruled out? Third rung: the ladder is cut to six rungs with a small number in the tray and the child climbs it from the foot with no rung skipped. The number pad stays open.

wrong.why: nothing in a written list says which numbers were tried, so a run with a hole in it comes out looking exactly like a run without one, and the child who skipped is never contradicted by the page.
wrong.move: jumps from two straight to four, because three has an odd look to it and the run is long.
wrong.screen: the ladder refuses to open the fourth rung and lights the third, naming it and giving nothing else away. When the third rung is taken it comes out at once, six rows of three with the shelf empty, and two cards drop into the pen. The pen is then read out with those two cards lifted and standing to one side, so that the list the skip would have produced and the list the run produced are up together.

wrong.why: a list of factors is what was asked for, so a row that produced no factor looks like a row not worth the ink, and the shorter page looks tidier.
wrong.move: keeps only the rungs that came out and leaves the failed trials off the paper altogether.
wrong.screen: two ladders are drawn side by side, one carrying every rung from one upward and one carrying only the rungs that lit. Both are read out and both give the same six numbers. A rung is then quietly taken out of the second ladder and it is read again: nothing on it has changed and nothing anywhere says a trial is missing. The first ladder keeps its blank rung lit.

phases.screen: the ladder from the foot upward with every rung blank and waiting
phases.soWhat: Work up from one and try every whole number in turn, and write down the trials that fail as well as the ones that come out.
phases.concept: Working up through the numbers in order

phases.win: two cards land in the pen from one rung and the pen count goes up by two
phases.does: reads the number stepped on and the number in each row, and drops both into the pen
phases.goal: one exact division puts two numbers into the list
phases.says: You made one division. How many factors has it just given you?
phases.check: 51 divided by 3 is 17. Which two factors of 51 has that one division handed you?
phases.feels: one sharing, and two cards land in the pen together
phases.hands: Lay twenty-seven counters out in three equal rows and ask for both numbers on the board to be said aloud, three rows and nine in each. Write both into the factor list. Then turn the board a quarter turn, so the same counters read as nine rows of three, and ask whether that is a new fact or the one already written. Do it again with fifty-six counters in seven rows and see how many entries one sharing is worth.
phases.tries: First rung, from the item: how many rows are on the board? Second rung, the phase's: how many are in each row, and is that a factor too? Third rung: the tray is cut to twelve things, the child steps on two, and both cards are dropped in by hand. The number pad stays open.

wrong.why: the rung is the thing the finger touched and the thing the question seemed to be about, while the number in each row arrives as the result of the work rather than as another answer.
wrong.move: writes down the number stepped on and lets the number in each row go, so the pen fills one card at a time.
wrong.screen: the board is turned a quarter turn in front of the child, the same twenty-seven counters reading as nine rows of three, and the ladder steps itself onto the ninth rung to show that rung coming out on the same tray. The card the child did put in the pen stays exactly where it was put, and the one that was let go is drawn lying on the board beside its row with the pen wall open beside it.

wrong.why: every rung produces a number stepped on and a number in each row whether it comes out or not, and the leftover sits off at the side of the board where it is easy to stop counting it.
wrong.move: drops two cards in for a rung where something was left over, because a division was still done and two numbers still came out of it.
wrong.screen: the leftover lights on its shelf and is counted out. The rows are counted beside it, four rows of six, and the board is read as twenty-four against a tray of twenty-seven. The two cards spring back out of the pen with nothing marked, the pen count drops back to what it was, and the rung is left standing as a failure with its three still outside the rows.

phases.screen: a rung that has just come out, with the empty pen beside it
phases.soWhat: Every division that comes out exactly gives you the number you divided by and the answer, and both of them are factors.
phases.concept: Every exact division hands you two

phases.win: the repeat light comes on, the ladder stops and the pen is read out as finished
phases.does: carries on climbing until a card lands on one already in the pen
phases.goal: the list is finished when the answers repeat what is already there
phases.says: Keep going. Tell me the moment an answer is one you have already written.
phases.check: You are finding the factors of 96, and 5 and 7 have both just failed. May you stop there? Say what you would lose.
phases.feels: the moment an answer is one you have already written, there is nothing new left to find
phases.hands: Climb forty-five on squared paper, a line for every whole number from one upward, and write both numbers of every division that comes out. Stop the moment somebody notices an answer they have already written and ring it. Then start on ninety-six and stop deliberately early, straight after six, because five and seven have both just failed. Write out the list as it stands, then carry the run on to the repeat and see which two numbers the early stop had lost.
phases.tries: First rung, from the item: which answer has just come out of the division? Second rung, the phase's: is that number already standing in the pen? Third rung: the ladder is cut to a small number and the child climbs it to the repeat and reads the pen out. The number pad stays open.

wrong.why: a run of trials that give nothing feels like the end of the number, and the list standing in the pen is long enough by then to look like an answer rather than like part of one.
wrong.move: stops after a couple of failures in a row and calls the list complete, because the pen already looks respectably full.
wrong.screen: the ladder carries on from where the child stopped, one rung at a time, with every rung that was never climbed lit in order as it is reached. The pen the child left is kept drawn exactly as it stood, beside the pen the finished run builds, and the two are read against each other card by card so that the cards the early stop never had are the only ones standing alone. Nothing is marked.

wrong.why: the ladder still has rungs on it and stopping while there is anything left to try feels like leaving the job half done, and a longer list looks like a better one.
wrong.move: keeps climbing past the repeat all the way to the number itself, writing every pair down a second time.
wrong.screen: the repeat light stays on and the ladder is allowed to climb. Every rung above the repeat does come out, and every card it sends lands on one already lying in the pen and is drawn settling on top of it rather than beside it. The pen count in the corner is held in view throughout and never moves, and the whole of the child's extra work stays drawn on the ladder.

phases.screen: the ladder well up with the pen already holding most of the list
phases.soWhat: Stop when the answers begin to repeat what is already in the pen, and not when the failures have made you tired.

writeup.delight: The third phase, at the instant a rung comes out. The rows settle level on the board and the two cards leave together, one lifting off the rung the child stepped on and one lifting off the end of a row, and they travel side by side along a drawn path into the pen and land as a linked pair. Drag either card back out and the other follows it, because the two came from one division and neither of them was found on its own. The count in the corner goes up by two on the way in and down by two on the way back, the rows on the board never move, and the voice says nothing at all while it happens.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing in front of it. On the first phase a full tray stands at the top of the ladder with exactly two rungs offered under it, one that will come out and one that will not, and the leftover shelf empty and ruled. On the second the ladder stands from the foot upward with every rung blank and the tray already loaded. On the third a single rung has just come out, its rows lying level on the board, with the factor pen beside it empty and its two end walls up. On the fourth the ladder is well climbed, most of the pen is full, and the repeat light above it is dark. The running count at the top left holds the rungs tried against the rungs the ladder is built for, with the count of cards in the pen beside them, and the answer slot and the pad stand empty down the right. One thing moves, once: the lower of the two offered rungs, or the rung at the foot, or the pair of numbers lying on the settled rows, or the next untried rung, gives one slow pulse while the voice asks what sharing the tray out that way would leave behind. That pulse is the only invitation, and a finger on it is the whole way in.
writeup.freePlay: Any number up to a hundred in the tray, with the pen, the leftover shelf and the repeat light switched on or off. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on testing a single divisor, working the run in order without skipping, reading two factors out of one division, and saying when the list is finished.
voiceLines: A tray of things up at the top, and a ladder of trials under it.
Share them out. Which try left nothing over? That one is a factor.
Start at the bottom and take every rung. Try to jump one and see what happens.
You made one division. How many factors has it just given you?
Keep going. Tell me the moment an answer is one you have already written.
Another number in the tray. Start at the foot and take every rung.
Free play. Any number in the tray, with the pen, the shelf and the repeat light as you like.
Share them out again, slowly. What is standing outside the rows?
Every rung tried in order, every failure still showing, and the pen full.

observations.why: A trial that fails rules a number out, and a number that was never ruled out is a number never tried.
observations.soWhat: The failures are part of the working, and a list with them rubbed out cannot be checked.
observations.observe: The trials that failed stayed on the ladder with their leftovers standing beside them.

observations.why: A number that is skipped can still be a factor, and nothing later in the run says it was missed.
observations.soWhat: The run starts at one and takes every whole number in turn.
observations.observe: The ladder would not open a rung while a lower one was still blank.

observations.why: The number divided by and the answer both divide the number exactly, so both are factors of it.
observations.soWhat: The list grows two at a time, and writing down only the divisor writes down half of it.
observations.observe: One exact division put two cards in the pen, never one.

observations.why: Past that point every pair is one already found with its two numbers swapped over.
observations.soWhat: The repeat is the stop signal, and running out of patience is not.
observations.observe: The pen stopped filling at the moment a card landed on one already inside.

phases.screen: a full tray with two rungs offered, one that comes out and one that does not
phases.win: one rung lights with level rows and the other leaves its remainder standing outside them
phases.traceback: The tray is shared again at walking pace on each rung; what will not fit goes to the shelf and stays, the rows are counted, and the rung that leaves nothing over is named.
ladder: Which of the two rungs sent something to the shelf?
After 8 rows, how many are sitting on the shelf?
Did every one of the 78 find a place in a row?
What does anything standing outside the rows say about this trial?
Count what sits on the shelf. A factor leaves the shelf empty.

phases.screen: the ladder from the foot upward with every rung blank and waiting
phases.win: every rung carries either level rows or a leftover, and no rung is blank
phases.traceback: The ladder climbs itself from the lowest blank rung, each trial keeping its rows or its leftover, and the rung the question asks about is named.
ladder: Look for the lowest rung that sent something to the shelf.
Is any rung on the ladder still blank?
What did each skipped rung leave on the shelf?
Can a number you never tried be ruled out?
Go back to the lowest blank rung before any other.

phases.screen: a rung that has just come out, with the empty pen beside it
phases.win: two cards land in the pen from one rung and the pen count goes up by two
phases.traceback: The cards still waiting travel into the pen one at a time, the rest of the ladder is climbed, and the pen is counted card by card.
ladder: The rung has given one card. What else came out of that division?
Is the answer to the division a factor as well?
Did both cards from rung 2 reach the pen?
How many are in each row, and is that a factor too?
Multiply the rows by the number in each. Do you get the whole tray back?

phases.screen: the ladder well up with the pen already holding most of the list
phases.win: the repeat light comes on, the ladder stops and the pen is read out as finished
phases.traceback: The ladder climbs on rung by rung until a card lands on its twin in the pen; the repeat light comes on and the pen is read as finished.
ladder: Which answer has just come out of the division?
Look at the pen. Which of those cards is also a rung you have not tried?
What happens at the rung where the rows and the number in each are the same?
Is that number already standing in the pen?
Look at the pairs on the lit rungs. When does a pair turn round?

ladder.record: each tried rung keeps its leftover, 0 over lit blue

model.tray: the number as counters, tens tied into rods

pen.twins: a repeat lands on its twin

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, nothing resets, no colour means good or bad. The child's answer stays; the pad re-opens after the traceback.
tracebacks: Phase 1: The tray is shared again at walking pace on each rung; what will not fit goes to the shelf and stays, the rows are counted, and the rung that leaves nothing over is named.
Phase 2: The ladder climbs itself from the lowest blank rung, each trial keeping its rows or its leftover, and the rung the question asks about is named.
Phase 3: The cards still waiting travel into the pen one at a time, the rest of the ladder is climbed, and the pen is counted card by card.
Phase 4: The ladder climbs on rung by rung until a card lands on its twin in the pen; the repeat light comes on and the pen is read as finished.

voice.opening: A tray of things to share, and a ladder of trials beside it.
voice.onMiss: the item's own miss line, then the phase's two ladder rungs
voice.onFinish: Every rung tried in order, every failure still showing, and the pen full.
voice.rules: Spoken on opening, as each phase begins, on each question, on a miss and on the summary page. Every line is printed in the bubble, numbers as words, by the device's own voice (Indian English first). Muting keeps the child's place; unmuting speaks on from the word it reached. If the browser refuses speech until a tap, the first line waits behind a Tap to start cover.

guide.playsOn: none: an Udgam tool opens straight on its phase; the phase's teach lines are spoken first, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

toolQuestions.source: props.questions ?? props.additionalProps?.questions is read; the authored rows below keep their stage (fitHost returns null).

items.planQuestion: Divide 20 by 4, then divide 20 by 6. Which of the two is a factor of 20?

question.en: Share 20 on each of the two rungs. Which of them is a factor of 20?

items.planAnswer: 4 is a factor of 20 and 6 is not

question.en: Is 8 a factor of 68? Step on the rung to find out.

items.planAnswer: No, because 68 divided by 8 is 8 with 4 left over

question.en: Now the tray holds 78. Is 6 a factor of 78?

items.planAnswer: Yes, because 78 divided by 6 is 13 with nothing over

items.planQuestion: Find every factor of 40 by dividing by each whole number from 1 upwards, and name the first trial that fails.

question.en: Find the factors of 40, one rung at a time from the foot. Which is the first rung that fails?

items.planAnswer: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20 and 40, and the first trial that fails is 3

items.planQuestion: Find every factor of 92 by dividing in turn.

question.en: Now find every factor of 92 by dividing in turn. Press enter when every rung is done.

items.planQuestion: A child finding the factors of 70 divides by 1, then 2, then jumps straight to 5. Which trials were skipped, and what would they have shown?

question.en: A child finding the factors of 70 jumped from 2 straight to 5. Step on the rungs that were skipped. Were any of them factors?

ask.en: Which skipped rung is a factor?

items.planAnswer: 3 and 4 were skipped. 70 divided by 3 leaves 1 over and 70 divided by 4 leaves 2 over, so neither is a factor

items.planQuestion: 27 divided by 3 is 9. How many factors of 27 has that one division handed you?

question.en: 27 divided by 3 is 9. How many factors of 27 has that one division handed you?

items.planQuestion: 51 divided by 3 is 17. Name the two factors of 51 that this one division gives.

question.en: 51 divided by 3 is 17. Drop the factors this one division gives into the pen, then press enter.

items.planQuestion: 62 divided by 2 is 31. Which two factors does that give, and how many factors has 62 altogether?

question.en: 62 divided by 2 is 31. How many factors has 62 altogether?

items.planAnswer: 2 and 31, and 62 has four factors: 1, 2, 31 and 62

items.planQuestion: Climb the ladder for 45 and say at which rung the answers begin to repeat.

question.en: Climb on for 45. At which rung do the cards begin to repeat?

items.planAnswer: At 9, because its answer 5 is already in the pen, and the factors are 1, 3, 5, 9, 15 and 45

items.planQuestion: Find every factor of 76 by dividing in turn, and say at which trial the answers begin to repeat.

question.en: Now the tray holds 76. Which rung is the first to send a card that is already in the pen?

items.planAnswer: 1, 2, 4, 19, 38 and 76, and they begin to repeat at 19, whose answer 4 is already on the list

items.planQuestion: A child says 100 has an odd number of factors. Find them all and say whether that is right.

question.en: A child says 100 has an odd number of factors. Climb on and count them. How many does 100 have?

items.planAnswer: Yes. 100 has nine factors, 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50 and 100, and the run stops at 10 because 10 tens make 100

scoring.wrong: costs nothing, never marked, counted only for first try accuracy
scoring.stars: one for finishing, two at sixty per cent right first time, three at ninety; hidden with the first-try line by showScore false
scoring.phaseMount: a mount scores every phase it plays, from its phase to the last (+5 a question; phases of 3, 3, 3, 3 questions)
scoring.finishCard: stars and the Right first time line under the phase rows on the summary page

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 4; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 4 to the summary page; finished once, from the summary page.
hostContract.navigableDots: true (or no phase): user mode, the phase dots are controls; otherwise AI mode, the dots show progress and the agent drives window.toolApi.

onProgress.done: questions right so far in this phase

hostContract.emits: every event is dispatched on window and, when framed, posted to window.parent as { type: 'event', name, detail }

terminalEvent.fires: once per mount, from the summary page after the last phase, 5 s after the page opens (its lines may still be going on); one-shot guarded and re-armed by restart or Play again; never sent at the end of an earlier phase (the tool walks on), and never if Free play or Play again is tapped first

sounds: Web Audio, no files: correct, wrong (soft), win, and a tick when a piece snaps

voiceLines.en: A tray of things up at the top, and a ladder of trials under it.
Share them out. Which try left nothing over? That one is a factor.
Start at the bottom and take every rung. Try to jump one and see what happens.
You made one division. How many factors has it just given you?
Keep going. Tell me the moment an answer is one you have already written.
Another number in the tray. Start at the foot and take every rung.
Free play. Any number in the tray, with the pen, the shelf and the repeat light as you like.
Share them out again, slowly. What is standing outside the rows?
Every rung tried in order, every failure still showing, and the pen full.
